column13:
Does CT use common formative assessments?
3 – Advanced
The CT consistently develops and uses multiple common formative assessments across units. Assessments are aligned to standards, given at agreed-upon times, and results are regularly analyzed collaboratively to inform instruction and interventions.
2 – Developing (Progressing)
The CT uses some common formative assessments, but not consistently across all units or courses. There is partial alignment and occasional collaboration in reviewing results, though practices may vary among team members.
1 – Beginning (Progressive)
The CT rarely or inconsistently uses common formative assessments. Assessments are mostly individual, with little alignment or shared analysis of student data.
column14:
Does CT use assessment data to adjust instruction?
3 – Advanced
The CT uses assessment data to adjust instruction for most or all (75–100%) units or learning cycles. Instructional changes are timely, targeted, and consistently implemented across the team based on shared data analysis.
2 – Developing (Progressing)
The CT uses assessment data to adjust instruction for some (25–74%) units or learning cycles. Adjustments are occasional and may vary by teacher or unit, with inconsistent follow-through.
1 – Beginning (Progressive)
The CT uses assessment data to adjust instruction for few or no (0–24%) units or learning cycles. Instructional decisions are rarely informed by shared data or are made individually without team alignment.
